mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above the prior month's level coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity payoffs.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above its previous month's value by at least 0.25 percentage points
failure_condition: In rising-rate regimes, the 20-day forward return is non-negative in at least 80% of triggered events, or the 5-day realized volatility of SPX does not exceed the 20-day forward volatility.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in unemployment claims accompanied by a simultaneous decline in industrial production signals weakening labor market strength and contracting supply, leading to negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises by at least 2% while INDPRO falls by at least 1% in the same month
regime_hint: Early signs of labor market softening
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, the 60-day forward return is positive in >50% of such labor-market signal events, or the correlation between the signal and returns falls below -0.2.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in home sales (HOUST) accompanied by a decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) suggests improving demand conditions without cost pressures, predicting a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by at least 5% month-over-month while CPIAUCSL decreases by at least 0.2% over the same month
failure_condition: In 20% of such demand-improvement events, the 20-day forward return is negative or the Sharpe ratio of the return does not exceed the 5-day realized volatility of SPX by at least 0.1.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in manufacturing activity (INDPRO falling by >5% month-over-month) in the absence of a corresponding decline in employment (PAYEMS) indicates supply-side weakness, producing a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >5% while PAYEMS remains flat or rises
regime_hint: Isolating supply shock without labor market adjustment
failure_condition: Over 30 such supply-contraction events, the 5-day forward return is non-negative in more than 70% of cases, or the Granger causality from INDPRO to SPX returns fails to hold.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 4.5% and coincides with a sustained decline in the 12-month change in consumer prices (CPIAUCSL), it suggests a robust labor market and disinflation, leading to a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.5% AND CPIAUCSL 12m change < -0.5% in the same month
failure_condition: In 40% of such regime events, the 60-day forward return is negative, or the return's beta to UNRATE is not statistically significantly different from zero (t-test p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in job openings (not directly observable in the provided proxies) would typically be accompanied by rising payrolls (PAYEMS) and falling unemployment (UNRATE); when PAYEMS rises by >10% while UNRATE falls by >0.3%, it signals strong labor demand and supports a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% while UNRATE decreases by >0.3% in the same month
failure_condition: Across 50 such labor-demand spikes, the 20-day forward return is negative in more than 40% of events, or the return's sensitivity to PAYEMS (beta) is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A month-on-month rise in retail sales (HOUST) with no decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) suggests resilient demand, predicting a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return in a non-stagflationary macro regime.
failure_condition: In 30 consecutive months with such demand signals, the 5-day forward return is negative in more than 50% of months, or CPIAUCSL shows a >0.5% monthly increase while HOUST rises by <2%.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of at least 3 consecutive months without a concurrent drop in unemployment (UNRATE) suggests structural supply constraints, resulting in a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for 3 consecutive months while UNRATE remains flat or rises
regime_hint: Structural supply shock without labor market adjustment
failure_condition: Over 100 such multi-month supply contractions, the 20-day forward return is positive in more than 60% of cases, or the shock's effect on SPX returns is not statistically significant (Granger causality p > 0.1).
